claim: For the Zolfaghari-Nejad–Charmi–Hassanpoor flow at the parameter vector used in the introducing paper to display chaos, \( (p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4,p_5,p_6,p_7)=(3.964,7,7,5,4.5,2.9,1) \), there exists an equilibrium in the box \[B=[1.002723,1.004723]\times[0.746237,0.748237]\times[-0.394482,-0.392482].\] This equilibrium is off the reported axis \(x=y=0\) and is hyperbolic with exactly one eigenvalue of positive real part and two eigenvalues of negative real part. A Poincaré–Miranda certificate for a rationally preconditioned vector field proves existence, and interval bounds on the characteristic coefficients throughout \(B\) give \(a_1>0\), \(a_2>0\), and \(a_3<0\) for \(\lambda^3+a_1\lambda^2+a_2\lambda+a_3\). Therefore the published parameter set is not a system whose equilibria are only the nonhyperbolic points \( (0,0,k\pi) \); in particular the paper's central equilibrium classification is incomplete. No claim is made here about the total number of omitted equilibria, uniqueness in \(B\), or the global attractor structure.
integrity: Existence is proved by a Poincaré–Miranda sign certificate using exact rational interval arithmetic and standard-library Taylor enclosures. Hyperbolicity follows from interval bounds on the full characteristic coefficients over the certified box. Numerical root-finding was used only to locate a candidate box and is not part of the proof.
limitations: The theorem certifies at least one off-axis hyperbolic equilibrium for the paper's displayed chaotic parameter vector. It does not count all equilibria, prove uniqueness in the certified box, or classify the paper's attractor basins.
title: An omitted hyperbolic equilibrium in a sine–cubic chaotic flow
